Home Editors Pick Agentic AI Google AI Releases Elephant-Goldfish Model Plugin for Spec-First Coding [...] Google has open-sourced the Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) plugin, a design-and-review layer for AI coding agents. The Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin makes an agent write a specification before it writes code. Fresh subagents with no conversation history then attack that spec. Google says thousands of its engineers use it. It is quite simple: catch wrong assumptions in a Markdown file, not in a pull request.

Those attempts followed September attacks that chained two SMA1000 zero-days to achieve remote code execution, as well as July attacks that exploited two other zero-days to deploy malware on vulnerable appliances. [...] # SonicWall warns of new SSL-VPN MFA bypass flaw exploited in attacks

SonicWall has released security updates to fix seven vulnerabilities in SonicOS firewalls, including an SSL-VPN authentication bypass flaw exploited in attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-19868, allows attackers with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method to bypass SAML authentication controls, potentially including SAML-enforced multi-factor authentication (MFA). [...] While SonicWall has not shared details about the reported exploitation, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added CVE-2026-19868 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, confirming that the flaw has been exploited in the wild.

CISA ordered federal civilian executive branch agencies to secure affected systems by November 20, 2026.

title: Microsoft Paint flaw allows remote code execution | Cybernews
body:
Microsoft was forced to address a vulnerability in Microsoft Paint, titled CVE-2026-83844, that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely.

The vulnerability was put in the high-severity category with a score of 8.1 8.1 CVSS 3.1. Despite this, Microsoft had classed it as "important," which felt a few shades less serious. [...] Additionally, the flaw was classified as a CWE-125, known as an out-of-bounds read, meaning software accesses memory outside the boundaries of a buffer.

For example, if a program were told to read boxes 1-10, the malicious error exposed potentially sensitive errors in box 11, which could contain sensitive information.

title: OpenAI Jalapeño AI chip challenges Nvidia in inference
body:
Nvidia's near-monopoly over the most advanced AI chips is under "threat" as OpenAI's and other tech giants announce custom-built semiconductors, analysts told CNBC.

OpenAI announced that its first AI chip, the Jalapeño, had "industry-leading speed and efficiency," as it unveiled the semiconductor on Tuesday. Google, AWS and Meta are all also developing their own AI chips. [...] Nvidia has been approached for comment.

OpenAI announced the first benchmarking results from its Jalapeño, saying it would allow users to get "faster responses, more responsive agents and more reliable access" as demand grows.

The new chip is being developed with Broadcom. It will be deployed within OpenAI's compute infrastructure by the end of the year, and OpenAI said it was already working on the semiconductor's generations two and three. [...] The Jalapeño chip, designed for inference, shows that a "hyperscaler-designed chip can now match or beat Nvidia's Blackwell-class GPUs on inference efficiency," Adrien Sanchez, technology analyst at Yole Group, told CNBC.

He added that, while Nvidia still owns the "vast majority" of AI compute and has ecosystem lock-in to its software platform CUDA, OpenAI's new chip is a "threat to Nvidia's inference margins, which is the field growing the most at the moment."

title: Meta releases Muse Ember, a new lightweight model for agent execution | TechCrunch
body:
Meta Superintelligence Lab released a new AI model on Monday called Muse Ember, the lab’s lightest and most cost-efficient AI model yet. In its release, Meta said Ember was “designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.” [...] Ember is the fourth model released under Meta’s Muse brand, following the mid-weight Spark (released in April), Spark’s open-source twin Glimmer (released in August), and the Wonder frontier model (released in October). The flagship consumer AI product, the Muse Agent, was released in September to unexpected success, with new features like Spaces and video chat rolling out earlier this month.

Topics [...] Given the emphasis on low cost and accuracy at scale, Ember is designed to pair with a larger model like Meta’s Muse Wonder in an agentic harness. In the case of a customer-support agent, for instance, you might see a heavier model establishing rules for how to handle a particular issue, then sending a lighter-weight model to apply the rules across tens of thousands of cases. As Meta puts it in the announcement, “Muse Wonder plans, Muse Ember handles the volume.”

The semiconductor industry is the posterchild for geopolitics and its challenges. Advanced chip production is geographically concentrated. Advanced memory production across South Korea, Japan, and Taiwan represent a concentrated “ring of fire” for supply chain disruption, while Taiwan controls 90% of advanced semiconductor production, mainly through TSMC.3 Correspondingly, supply-contract conversations with tech hardware companies have shifted from “beat this price” to “show me the resilience [...] Technology decisions are becoming geopolitical decisions as AI, semiconductors, data and critical infrastructure increasingly intersect with national security, reshaping technology partnerships and supply chains.
 Sovereignty is creating new areas of structural demand, directing capital towards domestic AI capabilities, regionalised supply chains, power, networking, cybersecurity and other enabling infrastructure. [...] For most of the past three decades, technology decisions have been commercial decisions: companies would buy the most appropriate system, at the best price, with the domicile of the supplier a secondary detail. title: The Chip War Explained: Supply Chain Risks Every Tech Leader Should Map - TechStoriess.com
body:
SHARE

Most executives still file the chip war under geopolitics: a contest between Washington and Beijing that someone in government will eventually settle. That framing is a mistake. For a CIO, CFO, or COO, it is a procurement problem. It shows up as delayed server deliveries, a license that changes mid-contract, and a laptop refresh that costs more than the budget assumed.

Contents [...] The foundation of the current regime is US export control law. The Foreign Direct Product Rule extends US jurisdiction to foreign-made products that derive from US technology, even when the finished chip contains no US content. That reach is why a restriction written in Washington can stop a shipment between two other countries. [...] ## Conclusion

The chip war will not end with a treaty that returns the old, predictable market. The more useful assumption is a permanent contest in which rules shift, supply is allocated by whoever pays most, and the biggest dependencies sit several tiers below your vendor. Companies that map those tiers now will make better decisions when the next announcement lands. The rest will learn about their exposure from a delivery notice.

title: The Geopolitics of Trade Infrastructure - Middle East Institute
body: For the US, this creates both leverage and a dilemma. American companies occupy pivotal positions in global commerce, and Washington can influence access to advanced technology. Yet that centrality leaves US firms, supply chains, and partners exposed when systems fail or become targets. Control over a chokepoint is not the same as security; concentrated dependencies can become sources of coercion. [...] The UAE’s partnership with Microsoft and AI and cloud computing firm G42 illustrates both the opportunity and the dependence. Microsoft has announced major investment in the country, including a stake in G42. In November 2025, US authorities authorized exports of advanced computing chips to G42 and Saudi Arabian AI company HUMAIN, subject to security and reporting requirements.
